gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the EG4 off-grid 'all-in-one' units cap output on each 120 V leg at half their nameplate (6000XP: 3,000 W per leg; 12000XP: 6,000 W L1-N or L2-N against 12,000 W L1-L2), with no load balancing between legs, so a 120 V-heavy panel can overload one leg while total load is well under the rating.
standout_why: I checked the four cited pages. EG4's 12000XP product page lists 12 kW split-phase and 24 kW PV but has no per-leg figure. Current Connected's /eg4-inverters guide gives 6000XP and 12000XP totals only. Eco Solar Kits' EG4 vs Sol-Ark guide says only that all models are '120/240V split-phase inverters that can run 240V loads' and does not cover unbalanced load. The Signature Solar user manual PDF did not appear in my fetches; the EG4-hosted manual and spec-sheet PDFs I fetched came back as unreadable binary. Among the uncited top results, liveoffthegrid.com/specs/inverters and sunforgelab.com give no per-leg limit. signaturesolarsolutions.com has idle draw but no per-leg limit. wildjoule.com (rank 13, uncited) mentions a '3,000 W-per-leg limit' for the 6000XP in passing. No page gives the 12000XP's 6,000 W per-leg cap or the no-balancing behaviour.
decides: This confirms the 6000XP as the pick only for small or 240 V-balanced off-grid loads. ChatGPT's '6 kW, 120/240V' card really means 3 kW available to any one 120 V circuit group. A cabin or home with mostly 120 V loads (fridge, microwave, space heater and well pump on one leg) is better served by the 12000XP (6 kW per leg) or by two paralleled 6000XPs, if the panel can't be balanced. It also makes 'is my load split evenly across L1 and L2?' a question the page should ask before naming any split-phase pick.

findings.label: Continuous output per 120 V leg
findings.value: 3,000 W per leg (6,000 W total at 120/240 V split-phase)
findings.note: Page text: 'each 120V leg carries up to 3,000W' and '6,000W continuous at 120/240V split-phase'. This is a retailer product page, not the cited /eg4-inverters guide. I tried EG4's spec sheet first (eg4electronics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/EG4-6000XP-Inverter-Spec-Sheet.pdf), but it came back as unreadable compressed binary.

findings.label: Idle draw
findings.value: about 50 W on battery; under 30 W on solar only
findings.note: Page text: 'Idle draw under 30W on solar and about 50W on battery'. At 50 W × 24 h = 1.2 kWh/day from the battery.

findings.label: Battery-free operation and grid export

findings.note: Page text: 'EG4 lists battery-free operation in off-grid mode' and 'an off-grid inverter that uses the grid for battery charging and pass-through, not export.'
